newsitem.title: CHINA: China paper warns investors on interim results.
newsitem.headline: China paper warns investors on interim results.

text.p: Chinese investors should be wary of 1997 interim results due to released by listed firms because they are unaudited and not representative of a full year's performance, the Business News said on Wednesday.
Optimism about the results, which must be released by August 31, had already pushed up share prices on China's two bourses in the past few days, the newspaper said in a commentary.
"But most of the interim results will not be audited and their authenticity cannot be compared with the annual reports of listed companies," it said.
"Past experience has proved that many listed firms have included part of their second half's profits in the interim results," it said.

China's securities rules do no require listed firms to audit their interim results, with the exception of those firms that have posted net losses for the preceding two years or intend to issue interim dividends.

The newspaper said the average price earnings (P/E) ratio of Shanghai-listed firms was now around 40 times and that some improvement in the firms' interim results could not sustain such a high P/E ratio.

In addition, prices of some domestic A share companies, including Shenma Industry Co and Zhenzhou Beiwen Co, had been pushed up by expectations of strong interim results, underlining future risk, Business News said.
The A share indices on both the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges recorded rises on Tuesday, while B shares fell slightly as profit-taking pared the gains of a recent rally.
